threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep confusing the Dalston Junction and Dalston Kingsland overground stops. Locals know which one’s the right one for a late-night kebab run.
Caught a night bus home last week and saw a guy in a full chicken costume arguing with a pigeon over a chip. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids playing street soccer while their parents bickered about the best kebab place on the corner. Pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip coffee next to a guy painting a mural while a kid rides by on a skateboard with their dog. It's a chaotic kind of normal.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name the taqueria that’s best at 3 AM and why the burritos change on Wednesdays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a street performer on the 8 bus today; he turned the whole ride into a sing-along. Only in SF do you get unexpected concerts on your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's only about the squares; they miss the tiny shops that open at weird hours and vanish with the sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order a 'café con leche'—too much emphasis on every syllable, like it's an art form.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'notting hill' party instead of a 'house gathering' — makes it clear you’re not yet in the local groove.
Caught a guy in a flat cap trying to negotiate a deal for leftover chicken on the 133. The driver just shook his head, amused.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a street musician playing accordion for a group of toddlers dancing around a fountain in Hasenheide, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Späti that doubles as a mini art gallery, showcasing local artists’ work right next to the beer fridges.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know that the BART delays mean planning around the 24-hour taco spot, not just the train schedule. We adapt, they wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit feeding a pigeon while waiting for the bus. He looked more at peace than anyone on their phone around him.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals flock to Park Güell, but on a sunny day, you’ll find us lounging in the secret corners of Plaça de la Vila.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they still search for the pause button on the metro when it stops unexpectedly. We're all used to it by now.
